description: What watches what. Four built-in managers and two regex ones:
github-actions -- every `uses:` ref under .github/, SHA-pinned with a
trailing # vX.Y.Z comment as they already are, plus
the node-version handed to actions/setup-node
swift          -- the version ranges in Package.swift (majors only,
see below)
regex          -- the pins in Package.resolved
mise           -- every tool in mise.toml
regex          -- the two hk package URLs in hk.pkl
npm            -- Playwright and axe-core in visual/package.json and
its lockfile
Package.resolved needs a regex manager because this package declares
swift-tools-version 5.5, so SwiftPM writes the lockfile in its version 1
format, and Renovate's swift manager only rewrites version 2 and later.
Left to itself it would also raise the `from:` floor in Package.swift on
every upstream release -- its default range strategy is `bump` -- which
is wrong for a package that ships a library product: consumers would
inherit a minimum nobody chose. So the two halves are split. The swift
manager runs with rangeStrategy `replace` and speaks up only when a
release falls outside the declared range, which is a major. The regex
manager moves the version and revision in Package.resolved for
everything. Both name a dependency the same way (owner/repo), so a major
lands as one pull request touching both files. If the tools version is
ever raised to 5.6 or later, the lockfile format changes and the regex
stops matching, so nothing would move the pins for in-range releases:
under `replace` the swift manager sees those as already satisfied and
never reaches its own lockfile code. At that point delete the regex
manager AND the rangeStrategy rule together. The swift manager's
default `bump` then updates Package.resolved itself, at the price of
raising the `from:` floor with each release.
Not covered, on purpose:
The Xcode versions in the workflow matrices (`latest-stable`, "16",
15) and the macos-15 image paired with them. They are the support
policy -- newest plus one major back -- not a pin gone stale, and
toolchain-drift.yml is what watches Xcode.
The release tags in scripts/version-compare. Those are this project's
own releases, chosen as comparison columns.
Homebrew. No formula is pinned anywhere; mise.toml exists because
Homebrew cannot pin the linters.
The sample app. It has no package dependencies.
Grouping and schedule carry over from the Dependabot config this
replaces: one run a week on Monday, minor and patch bumps of an
ecosystem as one pull request so a quiet week is one review, majors
separate because they are the ones that break things.
The three-day minimumReleaseAge is a supply-chain hedge: a release
pulled or re-tagged within days of publication never gets proposed.
Nothing automerges, by choice. main's ruleset needs 0 approvals and
the required checks, so automerge could work; it is not switched on.
Package.resolved, version 1 format. Captures the version and the
revision together so both move in one edit. extractVersion strips
a leading v because the lockfile records 1.2.2 even where upstream
tags v1.2.2 (XCResultKit does).
The hk version in hk.pkl, which appears twice in each of two package
URLs and has to match the hk entry in mise.toml. Named `hk` so it
shares a pull request with that entry.
Package.swift changes only when a release falls outside the
declared range. See the note at the top.

description: Actions: minor and patch releases as one pull request, along with
digest moves -- a tag that now points at a different commit than
the one pinned.
Everything mise.toml pins, and hk.pkl with it, as one pull request.
The lint jobs install these together, and hk's version has to move
in mise.toml and hk.pkl at once or the hook stops evaluating.

description: Leave the macOS and Xcode `runs-on:` labels alone. Renovate reads
macos-15 as a runner version and would offer macos-26, but that
image is there on purpose: it is the one that ships Xcode 16, the
older leg of the build matrix. Moving it is a support-policy
decision. Ubuntu labels are not matched, so a pinned ubuntu-24.04
gets its next image as a pull request rather than as a red check.
